notes: SNDK is an unusually extreme regime this quarter: trailing GAAP P/E ~24x (TTM diluted EPS $73.47) despite a 43x 12-month price move, because NAND-flash gross margin exploded from 7.1% (FY2023 trough) to 84.6% (FQ4 FY26) on a genuine industry-wide NAND supply shortage (AI-datacenter demand meeting underinvested 2023-24-era capacity). Forward P/E on FY2027 consensus is only ~7.7x at the current price — cheaper than every named peer except MU. This is squarely earnings-driven, not multiple-driven: the multiple has stayed structurally low (single-digit to low-teens) throughout the entire rally. Two live, unresolved risks worth carrying forward: (1) the pull-forward question — NAND-Research's own March/May 2026 updates explicitly describe 'panic buying' and downstream 'inventory buildup' in NAND specifically, which is genuinely in tension with the $93.9B/10-agreement supply backlog's multi-year visibility; no order-to-shipment or buyer-inventory-days metric was found to resolve this cleanly, so the backlog-cancellation KPI is the named tell. (2) The market already tested the bear case once: SNDK round-tripped from $2,335 (Jun 25, 2026 near-high) to $1,015 (Jul 29 low) on a 'memory supply-glut fear' scare that also hit STX/WDC/SK Hynix (Aug 3, -5% to -11%), before partly recovering to today's $1,568.87 — this dislocation is still unresolved (price has not yet reclaimed the $1,850 base floor) as of this snapshot.
